title: Amazon Stock (AMZN) Falls 3.9% After Anthropic IPO Debut (Nov 19)
summary: Amazon (AMZN) fell 3.87% to $257.37 on Nov 19 as stocks slid after the Nasdaq debut of Anthropic, in which Amazon holds a 14.6% stake.
body_markdown:
## Why Amazon Stock Fell


Yahoo Finance's live market coverage linked the afternoon slide to Anthropic's first day of trading. Anthropic[priced its IPO at $83 per share](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/anthropic-ipo-prices-83-raises-81-billion/) and began trading at $111.50, 34.3% above that price. Stocks moved lower after that first trade, and Amazon and Alphabet, the largest publicly traded companies with disclosed stakes in Anthropic, also dipped, according to[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-thursday-november-19-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-anthropic-ipo-live-141306032.html) .


Later in the afternoon, Vanda Research said retail investors sold single stocks to fund their Anthropic purchases, rotating out of AI names, Yahoo Finance reported. Anthropic closed its first session about 17% above its[initial public offering](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-an-ipo/) price after paring early gains.


Amazon had started the day higher. According to Anthropic's final prospectus, as reported by[GuruFocus](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/amazon-stocks-rise-1-82-173406464.html) , Amazon will hold 1,936,452,353 Class N shares, or 14.6% of Anthropic's outstanding share capital, making it the largest single holder. At the $83 offer price, GuruFocus calculated that stake at roughly $161 billion.


After the 4:00 p.m. close,[Bloomberg](https://finance.yahoo.com/small-business/articles/nyc-lawmakers-weigh-overhaul-amazon-220406127.html) reported that New York City lawmakers are weighing changes to a bill that would require Amazon to directly hire thousands of delivery workers. That report landed after the session ended.


## AMZN Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Anthropic committed to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon between May 2026 and April 2036, regardless of usage, according to GuruFocus.
- Amazon's 14.6% Anthropic stake was worth roughly $161 billion at the $83 offer price, per GuruFocus, and Anthropic ended its debut about 17% above that price, Yahoo Finance reported.


### Risks


- Selling in AI stocks hit Amazon on the day of the Anthropic debut, with Vanda Research pointing to retail investors rotating out of AI names to fund Anthropic purchases, as reported by Yahoo Finance.
- Chief executive Andy Jassy told CNBC that Amazon expects about $220 billion of capital spending this year and "meaningfully more" next year, per GuruFocus, which calculated that the $110 billion Anthropic commitment averages about $11 billion a year.
- New York City lawmakers are discussing replacing the bill's direct-hire mandate with a menu of options, and if an agreement is reached the legislation could come up for a vote within a few weeks, Bloomberg reported.
